newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Zalm says EU states "wise" to take time over EMU.
newsitem.headline: Zalm says EU states "wise" to take time over EMU.

text.p: Several European Union countries would be "wise" to take their time in qualifying for the planned EU single currency to ensure they can sustain their budget deficit to GDP ratios, Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said on Monday.

Zalm, who will chair meetings of EU finance ministers for the next six months, said the need to have sustainable deficits "probably will mean we will start (Economic and Monetary Union) with a smaller group of countries".

Briefing Brussels-based journalists at the start of the Dutch EU presidency, Zalm stressed that the EMU criteria of a public deficit of no more than three percent of Gross Domestic Product was the key element in meeting the requirements for a single currency.
"(Countries) should show that the way they reach a deficit like three percent is sustainable. It must be durable," he said.
Asked whether the EMU criteria set out in the Maastricht Treaty would be too strict to allow some countries to join, Zalm said: "There are a lot of countries that would be wise to take...more time."
He said that meant it was likely that a smaller, rather than a larger, group would qualify by January 1999.
Zalm played down the relative importance of some other criteria noting that the requirement of a public debt heading for below 60 percent of GDP was less important than the deficit requirement.
"The deficit is the root of all evil. Accumulating deficits make debt," he said.

He also said that he interpreted EU rules as not requiring countries to be in the bloc's Exchange Rate Mechanism for two years before joining a single currency, but only requiring them to have a stable exchange rate for two years.
Only Britain, Sweden and Greece are currently outside the ERM.
